title: Milvus vs pgvector: Scalability, Performance, Features
description: Milvus vs pgvector: compare retrieval performance, independent scaling and hot/cold tiered storage, with benchmark data and a Postgres-to-Milvus migration path.

h1: Milvus vs pgvector: a vector database comparison for growing data
intro: Milvus gives production vector search three dedicated advantages: specialized indexes and server-side hybrid retrieval, independently scalable ingestion/indexing/query resources, and tiered storage for hot and cold data. As the corpus grows, prioritize query-node memory and local disk for the active working set while retaining historical data in object storage. Keep Postgres for transactions, joins and business records; use Milvus to scale retrieval.

sections.h2: Milvus vs pgvector scalability: what happens when the table outgrows one Postgres box?
paragraphs: Milvus is built on storage-compute separation: segments and the write-ahead log live in object storage, a new query node loads its assigned segments instead of copying a disk, and ingestion, search and indexing scale on separate node types. Tiered storage lets a node serve data far beyond its memory.

pgvector scalability is Postgres scalability: scale up one instance, add hot-standby replicas (full copies, strictly read-only), or shard with Citus or PgDog, per the README. Every write and HNSW build runs on the primary. The documented behaviours:
bullets: HNSW build time and memory: fast while the graph fits maintenance_work_mem; past that Postgres warns "hnsw graph no longer fits into maintenance_work_mem" and builds take significantly longer. Parallel builds (0.6.0+) default to 2 workers; a 1M x 1,536-dim build took 60.10 min and 7,734 MB on r7gd.16xlarge (Jonathan Katz, 2023).
Indexable dimensions: vector up to 2,000, halfvec up to 4,000, bit up to 64,000.

Post-filtering recall cliff: at the default hnsw.ef_search of 40, a WHERE matching 10% of rows returns about 4 rows; iterative index scans (0.8.0+) rescan until k rows are found, up to hnsw.max_scan_tuples (20,000).
Index size vs memory: the README says indexes perform better in memory; AWS writes that an HNSW index must stay memory-resident or latency degrades.

sections.h2: Hot/cold separation: size retrieval resources for the active working set
paragraphs: Milvus Tiered Storage (2.6.4+) separates QueryNode caching from loading. Durable data stays in object storage; field chunks and segment indexes load on demand. Infrequently used cache entries can be evicted, while important fields and indexes can be warmed up.

For growing knowledge bases, historical documents and agent memory, this helps separate corpus capacity from active serving resources and reduce cold-data cache residency. pgvector also uses Postgres caching and disk-backed indexes; Milvus adds an object-storage-backed tiering mechanism designed for distributed vector retrieval.
bullets: Keep historical data searchable without keeping every field permanently resident on QueryNodes.
Scale query resources for traffic; size object storage and active cache for corpus growth.
sections.note: Cold accesses can add latency. Warm critical data or use full-load mode for strict latency targets. Savings depend on access patterns, indexes, cache hit rates and query requirements.

sections.h2: Why choose Milvus for production retrieval
paragraphs: Milvus combines specialized retrieval, independent scaling and hot/cold tiering in one service. Allocate resources by query, ingestion and indexing demand, and manage cache by access patterns. These controls matter when retrieval becomes a growing production workload rather than a small addition to an existing database.

sections.h2: What pgvector gives you that Milvus doesn't
paragraphs: pgvector's advantage is not the vector index; it is everything Postgres already does around the vector column. For a team whose data lives in Postgres these are reasons to stay, and a Milvus vs Postgres decision starts here.

sections.h2: Start on pgvector, move the vector table to Milvus: the polyglot pattern
paragraphs: The common path is not a replacement. Teams start on pgvector because the data is in Postgres, then move only the vector table to Milvus when it outgrows the primary, keeping Postgres for OLTP: users, orders, permissions, agent checkpoints. Rows and vectors join on the primary key; milvus vs postgres becomes Milvus and Postgres.

Is Milvus overkill for a small RAG prototype? Not with Milvus Lite, which runs in-process from pip install. Does Milvus require a GPU? No; GPU indexes are optional. The migration is a copy, not a re-embedding, through VTS (Vector Transport Service) and its pg_to_milvus config.

sections.h2: When is pgvector the better choice, and when Milvus? A decision checklist
paragraphs: pgvector is a well-maintained extension, and keeping vectors inside the database you already run is a real advantage. Is pgvector good enough for production RAG? For a single-tenant corpus on an existing Postgres, yes: it fits when the vector table fits one primary and you need transactions, JOINs or row-level security between embeddings and relational rows; agent memory with transactional updates is a good example, paired with Milvus for the large retrieval corpus. Teams searching for pgvector alternatives are usually hitting the single-primary behaviours above.

sections.h2: Which AI companies and enterprises run Milvus in production?
paragraphs: Milvus and Zilliz Cloud (managed Milvus) run in AI-native companies and large enterprises alike: the milvus.io adopter wall includes Salesforce, Walmart, NVIDIA, eBay, IBM, Cisco, Roblox and Reddit, alongside Exa.ai, OpenEvidence, Read.ai, Plaud and Filevine.

faqs: The table lists published results for all three systems, but instances, indexes and test periods differ. It does not establish a same-condition speed ratio. Benchmark with matching data, hardware, filters and recall targets.

The README sets no row limit; capacity is the primary's. AWS published a 367 GB HNSW index for LAION 100M (768 dims), built in 16.1 hours, serving 3.4 QPS cold on a 128 GB cache. Milvus Standalone is documented to about 100 million vectors, Distributed to tens of billions.

Yes: combine a vector query with Postgres full-text search (tsvector) and fuse results with Reciprocal Rank Fusion or a cross-encoder. Milvus runs BM25 server-side and fuses dense and sparse results in one hybrid_search call.
When should I use pgvector instead of Milvus?

When the vectors sit next to relational rows you join and update transactionally, the table fits one Postgres instance, and you want row-level security and SQL from one database. pgvector limitations (2,000 indexed dims, maintenance_work_mem-bound builds, full-copy replicas) decide the switch.
How hard is migrating from pgvector to Milvus later?

It is a copy. VTS ships a Postgres Vector source with a pg_to_milvus config, so embeddings and columns move without re-embedding. Map columns to scalar or JSON fields, build indexes, dual-write from the same source, and keep relational tables in Postgres.
